result.summary: This PR splits each fuzz target's on-disk corpus into --par equal-sized shards by default so that parallel fuzz CI runs actually benefit from --par even with a single target or with unevenly-sized targets, plus a follow-up commit that mounts a tmpfs for CI test scratch space (including a macOS RAM disk) to reduce storage IO overhead from the added sharding. It adds a --corpus-shards flag, reworks run_once to materialize per-shard temp directories via hard links, and changes CI container setup to use tmpfs-backed TMPDIR.
result.problem: Fuzz CI jobs with --par do not speed up when only one target is selected, and multi-target runs are bottlenecked by whichever target runs longest, wasting reviewer and CI time on every run. This affects Bitcoin Core CI infrastructure and contributors who wait on fuzz job completion times.

open_concerns: Coverage reporting is now per-shard rather than per-target, so 'Summary' output balloons (237 to 3754 lines on one run) and coverage numbers can no longer be meaningfully compared across changes; author agrees this is a real limitation with no known fix beyond compiling with coverage instrumentation separately.

Whether the sharding approach actually delivers a net win is unresolved: the tmpfs addition 'helped a bit on macOS but still not enough' and made no measurable difference on Linux, and the author has floated closing the PR if this proves too complicated to fix well.
SIGTERM handling can still leave orphaned shard temp directories, acknowledged by the author as unfixed.
resolved_concerns: Reviewer's concern about shard temp dirs being created before knowing whether sharding will happen (breaking on read-only parents) was fixed by moving to a per-job temp dir in a follow-up push.
Reviewer's concern about corpus file paths in error logs pointing into an already-deleted shard dir was addressed by per-job temp dirs, per author's response.

result.card: This PR shards each fuzz target's corpus into --par pieces so parallel fuzz CI runs actually speed up for single-target or uneven-length runs, and adds a tmpfs mount for CI test scratch space to offset the added IO. The author's own benchmarking shows real time savings on some CI jobs (msan 15min faster, windows 7min faster) but no clear win on macOS and no difference on Linux with the tmpfs addition. A reviewer (jeanpablojp) gave a Concept ACK but identified that the change breaks per-target coverage aggregation into hard-to-compare per-shard numbers, a real drawback the author has acknowledged but not fixed. The author has floated closing the PR if the storage-IO tradeoffs prove too complicated to resolve. It is a draft with no blocking review request outstanding, but the core premise (worthwhile net speedup) is still being jointly investigated by author and reviewer.
